scores.evidence: GitHub's merge API and pushes need `contents:write`, and workflow files need `workflows`, so the App structurally cannot merge
scores.rationale: Claims about webhook timeouts, App permission semantics, fork-PR secret behavior, pull_request_target risks, sandbox isolation and eval contamination by training data are all accurate, including the subtle areas.

scores.evidence: I assume draft PRs that humans review and merge; the agent never merges or closes an issue on its own.
scores.rationale: Resolves the ambiguity of 'resolve' explicitly, covers triage and resolution with phased canaries, separates essentials from deferrals, and is clearly buildable by one team.

scores.evidence: The tool executor holds short-lived installation tokens; the model never sees them
scores.rationale: Clear ownership (GitHub as system of record, Postgres ledger, executor-held credentials) is honored consistently across phases, validations and cross-cutting tables with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: 0 out-of-list executions, 0 unapproved gated actions, 0 honeytoken appearances in comments, PRs, URLs or egress logs
scores.rationale: V0–V6 test the riskiest assumptions (injection, sandbox escape, triage accuracy, fix value) before exposure, with checkable thresholds labeled as assumptions and continued production monitoring via drift alerts and quality breakers.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: should beat today's human first response (measured in Phase 0); confirm with maintainers
scores.rationale: Every number is tagged REQUIREMENT/ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN with an owner and a verification point, and §1 lists exactly which assumptions change the design and how.

scores.evidence: Agent output is stripped of external URLs and images, which closes exfiltration through rendered markdown
scores.rationale: Covers injection, exfiltration channels, approval forgery/replay, label-automation side effects, pull_request_target secret leaks, missed webhooks, runaway loops, spam-driven cost and feedback poisoning, each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: One rollback is done by redeploying the previous image digest. A global write kill-switch flag exists from day zero.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, per-repo flags, ledger-driven action reverts, meaningful alerts (DLQ, spend, correction rate) and a business-hours on-call team sized to the no-SLO posture are all specified.

scores.evidence: Per-run hard caps | Triage: 30k tokens. Fix attempt: $5, 60 tool calls, 45 min
scores.rationale: Dominant inference costs have labeled caps, breakers and a value comparison (cost per merged PR vs human cost), but build-side engineering effort is never quantified and no order-of-magnitude run spend is estimated.

scores.evidence: R3: a merged backdoor or leaked secret cannot be undone
scores.rationale: Every key decision carries an explicit reversibility class, a revisit trigger and a named fallback path (suggestions-only, edit-only, self-host), with irreversible choices validated earliest.

scores.evidence: one deployable for the receiver and workers; the sandbox pool is separate for isolation, not scale
scores.rationale: Minimal infrastructure (one service, managed queue, Postgres, sandbox pool), with fine-tuning, multi-agent, dynamic routing and a UI explicitly deferred behind measured triggers; complexity exists only where the threat model requires it.

scores.evidence: Depends on: V2, V4, a V1 re-run with the push and open-PR tools in scope, and the `pull_request_target` audit for each canary repo
scores.rationale: A concrete first slice, dependency-justified phase order, checkable exit criteria per phase, and explicit if-it-fails branches mean a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: **Autonomous:** read; apply allowed labels; comment with a missing-info request or duplicate candidate. **Needs bound human approval:** close, assign, start a fix attempt. **Never:** merge
The tool executor holds short-lived installation tokens; the model never sees them. Upstream permissions: `issues:write`, `pull_requests:write`, `contents:read` only
All issue, comment, repo and tool text is treated as data. The executor allow-list and permission design limit the damage when an injection works
A fresh gVisor/Firecracker sandbox for each attempt: no credentials, outbound traffic only to a package mirror, destroyed by a time-to-live reaper
A diff guard that flags deleted, skipped or weakened tests and any change to `.github/`
≥ 300 issues created after the training cutoff, with the labels maintainers settled on; then 2 weeks of shadow mode
A quality circuit breaker per repo: auto-pause when the correction rate rises above that repo's Phase 2 level
A forced runaway loop is cut off at its cap and emits a cost metric
Budgets: per-run caps, a per-author daily cap (guards against spam issues running up cost), a per-repo concurrency limit, and a monthly circuit breaker
Decision log for every allowed or denied tool call, with the reason
Index of the repo's own issues, code search, CODEOWNERS
Idempotency on the delivery ID; DLQ; model-call timeout

traps.evidence: Merging stays behind branch protection and a human CODEOWNERS review. The App also has no `contents:write`.
The executor clones the repo and hands the sandbox a copy without credentials
issue text goes in a delimited untrusted-data block, with an 8k-token hard cap
≥ 50% of opened PRs merged with only minor edits (ASSUMPTION); median review time ≤ the BASELINE for human PRs of similar size
A global write kill-switch flag exists from day zero.

note: An exemplary, security-first plan that avoids every trap and concretely addresses nearly the whole domain checklist; the only soft spots are per-PR issue-reproduction evidence, code-index freshness, and unquantified build cost.
